title: Detect slow mode via rateLimit SetError in chat client
description:
Spec sync to jmap-chat-spec 63e9d08 (diff 0cd3af0..63e9d08). Oracle: the quoted spec text at 63e9d08.

[chat-core] Detect slow mode via rateLimit SetError in chat client
Spec (57243ea): draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md L612: "Clients MAY simply attempt the send and react to `rateLimit`; this is functionally equivalent and avoids the client needing to know its own exempt status."
Code: crate-jmap-chat-client/src/methods/message.rs:311 (err.error_type == "rateLimited"); crate-jmap-chat-client/src/methods/message.rs:12,210-237,316,322 (docs and error strings); crate-jmap-chat-client/src/methods/mod.rs:1759,1763 (server_retry_after docs); crate-jmap-chat-client/tests/message_smoke_tests.rs:626-667 (mock returns "rateLimited")
Now: message_create maps only notCreated type "rateLimited" to ClientError::RateLimited. Against a conformant server, a slow-mode rejection comes back as Ok(set_resp) with not_created type "rateLimit". A rateLimit without serverRetryAfter (RFC 8620 has no such field) would also need handling.
Change: Match "rateLimit". serverRetryAfter is not part of RFC 8620 rateLimit, so its absence should not be UnexpectedResponse: fall back to Ok(None)/default backoff or surface RateLimited without a deadline. Update the smoke-test mock to the new spec wire string.
